projectTitle: AI SWOT and PESTLE Analysis Assistant
description: A student-sized VAC web application that accepts a business or project description and helps produce practical SWOT and PESTLE analyses.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Build an interactive browser UI with the requested HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use typed JavaScript for additional compile-time checks.

questions.question: Which frontend framework or approach do you prefer?
questions.recommendedChoice: Vanilla JavaScript with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap
questions.answer: Vanilla JavaScript with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap
questions.rationale: This directly matches the requested frontend technologies and keeps the student project straightforward.

options.label: Vanilla JavaScript with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap
options.description: A lightweight UI without an additional JavaScript framework.

options.label: React with Bootstrap
options.description: A component-based UI using React alongside Bootstrap.

questions.question: Which frontend features or constraints should the plan include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive form for a business/project description; generate clearly organized SWOT and PESTLE sections; allow editing and copying or downloading the results; include helpful validation and a concise, student-friendly interface.
questions.rationale: These features make the requested assistant practically usable while keeping the UI manageable for a student VAC project.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?

options.label: Python
options.description: Use Python for the analysis API and its application logic.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use JavaScript on the server as well as in the browser.

questions.question: Which Python backend framework do you prefer?
questions.rationale: Flask is a small, approachable framework suitable for a student-scale API; you can change this if you have a course requirement.

options.label: Flask
options.description: A minimal Python web framework with a small learning curve.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: A modern API-focused framework with request validation and generated API docs.

options.label: Django
options.description: A full-featured Python framework with an integrated ORM and admin tools.

questions.question: Which analysis behavior or AI integration should the backend provide?
questions.recommendedChoice: Generate a structured SWOT and PESTLE report from the submitted description. Specify whether the course requires a real AI provider/API or whether a transparent local/demo analysis is acceptable; do not put API keys in source code.
questions.rationale: The intended AI behavior and any provider requirement affect implementation, configuration, and project cost.

questions.question: Which data stores does the project need?
questions.rationale: A database was requested. SQLite is a practical, zero-service setup for a student project; review this if the course requires a hosted database.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: A lightweight relational database stored with the application, suitable for a local/student project.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: A relational database suitable for a hosted multi-user application.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: A managed relational database on Azure.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application API features?
questions.rationale: Sign-in was not requested; omitting it keeps the student project focused and simple.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users need accounts to access application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application is usable without user sign-in.
